record.title: OpenAI updates GPT-6 Luna with mixed safety-evaluation results
record.summary: OpenAI's October 29 system-card addendum identifies GPT-6 Luna (October 29) as an updated ChatGPT model, described as more concise and less overly agreeable than the October 7 version. The card assigns the update High capability classifications in cybersecurity and biological/chemical domains and reports 99.91% robustness on its instruction-hierarchy evaluation. OpenAI also reports improvement on four selected under-18 safe-completion evaluations, but mixed or lower comparisons on several HealthBench and MentalHealthBench measures. These are provider-run results; this review did not independently reproduce them or establish safety outcomes in ordinary use.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI published an October 29 system-card addendum identifying GPT-6 Luna (October 29) as an updated ChatGPT model. The card says the update is more concise and less overly agreeable and retains the October 7 model's training types and safeguards stack.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports that GPT-6 Luna (October 29) is High in cybersecurity and biological/chemical capability under its Preparedness Framework, and reports 99.91% robustness on its instruction-hierarchy evaluation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports improvement over the October 7 Luna snapshot on four under-18 safe-completion categories: sexual content, eating disorders, emotional reliance and gore. The reported scores are evaluation-specific and provider-run.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The October 29 addendum lists lower displayed values than the October 7 Luna column on HealthBench, HealthBench Hard, HealthBench Consensus and overall, non-acute and high-acuity MentalHealthBench, while the emergent MentalHealthBench value is slightly higher. These are provider-reported table comparisons, not a controlled longitudinal estimate: OpenAI says earlier-model values may reflect later model versions and can vary from previously published scores.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The provider-published card does not independently establish the reported safety or health-evaluation changes, their performance in ordinary deployment, or a broad improvement in model safety.

evidence_gaps.description: Safety, prompt-injection and health-evaluation values are provider-reported and not independently reproduced. The October 7 card says the difficult safety evaluations are not representative of average production traffic and that evolving policies, datasets and graders limit comparisons with earlier cards; the October 29 addendum also warns earlier-model values may reflect later versions.
The system-card comparisons do not establish safety or health performance under ordinary production traffic, deployment prevalence or downstream user outcomes.

brief.importance_rationale: A refreshed deployed assistant model and new provider-published safety measurements can inform model oversight and evaluation interpretation, though this is an incremental revision and its results are not independently established.
limitations: All comparative evaluation results and capability assessments are OpenAI-reported; no independent replication was performed.
The October 29 card inherits detailed evaluation-method descriptions from the October 7 card, which was not re-audited in this activation.
Provider metrics do not establish performance on ordinary production traffic or broad user safety outcomes.

Cross-version table differences are not a controlled longitudinal estimate: OpenAI warns that previous-model values may reflect later versions and vary from previously published scores; its October 7 card also says evaluation methods evolve and difficult safety-set error rates do not represent average production traffic.

The card assigns the update High capability classifications in cybersecurity and biological/chemical domains and reports 99.91% robustness on its instruction-hierarchy evaluation. technical.claimed_result: OpenAI reports a dated GPT-6 Luna behavior update, selected under-18 evaluation improvements and 99.91% instruction-hierarchy robustness, alongside mixed health-evaluation comparisons.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official system-card publication and its stated contents are established as a disclosure event. The underlying evaluation outcomes remain first-party claims.
technical.mechanism: The card describes a behavior refinement and retains the earlier Luna training types and safeguards stack; OpenAI attributes prompt-injection resilience to its adversarial GPT-Red training/evaluation approach.
technical.regime: OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna (October 29) ChatGPT update, evaluated on provider-run production, under-18, prompt-injection, HealthBench and MentalHealthBench sets. The card points to the October 7 card for detailed methods and notes comparisons may use later versions of earlier models. The October 7 card notes that safety evaluations use difficult cases without system-level safeguards, are not representative of average production traffic, and that methods change over time.
technical.reproducibility: The primary addendum is accessible and reports versioned comparisons. No independent reproduction was performed, and benchmark-method details were not re-audited in this activation. The October 7 card warns that previous-model values may reflect later versions and may vary from previously published scores, which limits longitudinal interpretation.
technical.strongest_baseline: OpenAI compares against GPT-6 Luna (October 7) and other listed GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6/GPT-6 snapshots. Several selected under-18 metrics improve, while HealthBench and most MentalHealthBench comparisons are mixed or lower. OpenAI cautions that earlier-model values can reflect later versions and vary from previously published scores; the table is descriptive provider reporting, not a controlled temporal comparison.

brief.title: OpenAI updates GPT-6 Luna with mixed safety-evaluation results
brief.why_it_matters: Dated model revisions can change the behavior and risk profile of widely deployed assistants. OpenAI's card gives a version-specific account of selected gains and trade-offs, but external evaluators still need to verify those measurements before drawing broader safety conclusions.
